reply.emotion: hurrying to get somewhere, tapping the steering wheel to the radio
notes: In Mexico and many other Latin American countries, 'carro' is the everyday word for a motor vehicle, much more common than 'coche'.
Do not confuse it with 'carro' in the traditional sense of a cart pulled by animals, which is less common in modern daily life.

senses.definition: Vehículo con cuatro ruedas y un motor que sirve para transportar personas por la calle.

examples.text: Dejó su carro estacionado enfrente de la casa.
examples.translation: He left his car parked in front of the house.
examples.emotion: pointing out where the vehicle is, practical and matter-of-fact

senses.definition: Vehículo sin motor de dos o cuatro ruedas que se empuja o se tira de él para llevar cosas.

examples.text: Llenó el carro del supermercado con mucha comida.
examples.translation: He filled the supermarket cart with a lot of food.
examples.emotion: pushing heavily loaded metal through a busy aisle, slightly tired
